sections.heading: Default parameters
sections.markdown: The function's throws clause bounds its body. Only omitted arguments evaluate their defaults and contribute escaping default errors to the call; explicitly supplied arguments skip those defaults. Throwing calls inside default expressions require their own try at the declaration, independently of the caller's propagation marker.

sections.heading: Parameter modes
sections.markdown:
- `name: T` is the default READ contract: the parameter cannot be rebound or directly mutate its value-semantic components, but copyable, storable values may be saved or returned as logical copies
- Copying stops at class and synchronized identity boundaries; a READ class parameter does not freeze the referenced object
- `name: ref T` is an exclusive writable place loan; calls must write `ref place`
- `name: move T` consumes a noncopyable resource according to the declaration; `move value` may explicitly mark that transfer. Copyable types, including Array, cannot declare move parameters or receivers
- Ordinary Array copying does not require `copy(array)` or unique backing. Type-position `const T`, the public `copy(array)` spelling, and standalone move expressions for copyable values remain outside the frozen subset
- Ordinary outputs use returns, tuples, or structs; business errors use typed throw/catch, without a global Result type

The new-XIR Array subset in spec §17.26 admits ordinary READ parameters, logical copies and returned values; a copied local var may mutate independently. Source ref parameters, move, and complete resource/view families still require separate admission.

sections.heading: Error signatures and external verification
sections.markdown:
- A named function without `throws` is non-throwing; `throws(Never)` is equivalent
- `throws(E)` is part of the signature; bare `throws` means `throws(Error)`
- Error checking is local to each body and uses callee signatures
- Propagating calls require `try`, or a `try { } catch` handling region
- Only the entry file may contain executable top-level statements. Entry-file top-level code and module-state initialization implicitly allow errors, with propagation markers; main is an ordinary function
- Throwing public standard-library APIs require typed errors, including constrained generics; freestanding and @strict(alloc) reject erased throws
- `xray verify` checks target artifact shape and no longer accepts `no_throw`

sections.heading: Higher-order functions
sections.markdown:
- Function types use `fn(T1, T2) throws(E) -> R`; omit throws for a non-throwing type and omit the arrow for Unit
- Error types are covariant by subset without changing parameter or result matching
- Generic `E: Error` is inferred from callback arguments; a non-throwing callback can infer `E = Never`
- Explicit closure throws clauses constrain the body before matching an expected type; otherwise closures use the expected type or local body inference
- fn lambdas may write throws(E); arrow lambdas do not write the clause
- Capture and cross-execution rules remain independent of the error signature
